Dizer a profissão: sem artigo, e o femin: Saying your job: no article, and the feminine in -in
PASSO 1: com «sein» (e «werden»), a prof: STEP 1: with «sein» (and «werden»), the job comes WITHOUT an article: «Ich bin Lehrer», not «Ich bin ein Lehrer» — even though English says "I'm a teacher". STEP 2: the feminine usually adds -in to the masculine: Lehrer → Lehrerin, Student → Studentin, Kellner → Kellnerin. English mostly uses one word for both ("teacher", "doctor"); German almost always marks a woman's job with -in. STEP 3: some words also take an umlaut: Arzt → Ärztin, Koch → Köchin. STEP 4: questions: «Was sind Sie von Beruf?» (formal), «Was bist du von Beruf?» (informal) or «Was machst du beruflich?» — "What do you do (for a living)?". STEP 5: another way to say it: «Ich arbeite als Verkäufer» (I work as a salesperson), also without an article — just like "work as". Careful: «Krankenschwester» (female nurse) has a different masculine: «Krankenpfleger».
o português também diz «sou professor» s: The English reflex "I'm a teacher" produces «Ich bin ein Lehrer», which sounds wrong. German drops the article before a job (unless there's an adjective: «Er ist ein guter Lehrer»). And where English has gender-neutral job titles, German usually has two forms: Lehrer / Lehrerin.
A profissão não leva artigo depois de «s: No article before a job after «sein» — unlike "I'm a teacher".
For a woman, the form is «Ärztin».

Onde você trabalha, passo a passo: Where you work, step by step
PASSO 1: pergunte «Wo arbeitest du?» ou: STEP 1: ask «Wo arbeitest du?» or «Wo arbeiten Sie?». STEP 2: to give the PLACE, use «in» and the forms you know from lesson 9: der and das words take «im» (im Büro, im Krankenhaus, im Geschäft); die words take «in der» (in der Schule, in der Fabrik, in der Praxis). STEP 3: to say WHO you work FOR, or at which company, use «bei» — English uses "at" or "for": «Ich arbeite bei Siemens» (I work at / for Siemens), «bei der Post», «bei der Bank». STEP 4: hours: «Ich arbeite von acht bis siebzehn Uhr» (from eight to five). STEP 5: ask «Wie lange arbeitest du?» (how long per day) and «Wann arbeitest du?» (what time). STEP 6: two common situations: «Ich bin arbeitslos» (I'm unemployed) and «Ich habe frei / Urlaub» (I'm off / on vacation). At A2 you'll see why it's «im» and «in der»; for now, memorize the pairs.
